saying: Nearly all commenters accept extending the competency-based approach to multimodal, world-model and other architectures, but ask that evaluation target the final configured device's behavior and function rather than its technical design, adding failure modes such as cross-modal consistency, error propagation and agentic authority. Two note benchmarks are thinner here and want clinical confirmation weighted more heavily.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on whether requirements should be architecture-neutral. Most want criteria anchored in intended function and device behavior, warning architecture-specific rules go stale; a few want the underlying architecture assessed in every case, with architecture-specific tests and higher risk categorization for vision-language models.

sides.summary: Keep evaluation architecture-agnostic, focused on the configured device's function, inputs/outputs and downstream authority.
Require architecture-specific assessment, tests and risk categorization tied to the underlying model type and modality.
